page: Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-amd is a virtual server instance within the High Performance product line, powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provisions 4 shared vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores utilizing multi-threading, paired with 12.0 GB of system memory, providing an allocation of 3.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is locally provisioned via a 260 GB NVMe SSD, and each instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address without dedicated hardware acceleration or discrete GPUs.

Benchmark testing reveals mixed compute and memory characteristics typical of shared-core configurations. The CPU demonstrated middle-tier capacity in synthetic stress testing, scoring 2,427.57 on single-core and 9,526.81 on multi-core stress-ng tests. In contrast, instruction throughput across Geekbench (1,110.0 single-core, 3,485.0 multi-core) and PassMark CPU tests (6,640.94) ranked in lower brackets. Memory subsystems displayed strong small-block cached read throughput of 380.64 GB/sec, but uncached throughput dropped significantly to 24.31 GB/sec for reads and 20.91 GB/sec for writes, contributing to lower rankings in PassMark memory scoring and data compression workloads.

The qualitative cost profile positions this instance favorably for resource-dense horizontal infrastructure that benefits from local NVMe storage without requiring sustained, dedicated CPU cores. Because execution resources are shared and large-block memory streaming is modest, intensive computational workloads and sustained high-IOPS database operations face definite bottlenecks. Consequently, this server is suitable for medium-traffic web serving, development and staging environments, lightweight microservices, and general-purpose background task processing.
description: Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-amd is an x86_64 virtual instance from the High Performance family featuring an AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The virtual machine allocates 4 shared vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 12.0 GB of system memory (3.0 GB per core), a bundled 260 GB NVMe SSD, and 1 complimentary public IPv4 address, with zero discrete GPUs. Benchmark results place stress-ng multi-core compute and cached memory bandwidth in average tiers, whereas sustained uncached memory throughput and Geekbench compute metrics settle in the lower quartiles. PassMark database and compression evaluations show moderate execution limits inherent to shared-thread environments. Qualitative efficiency remains advantageous for lightweight architectures demanding cost-effective local NVMe storage and balanced memory. The instance is suited for general application hosting, internal development environments, light microservices, and background utilities that do not require dedicated continuous compute cycles.
